name: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic
native: Беларуская Савецкая Сацыялістычная Рэспубліка (Biełaruskaja Saviecka Sacyjalistyčnaja Respublika)

predecessors.name: Russian Republic
predecessors.text: Cliopatria draws Belarus inside its Russian Republic shapes

ledger.x: 1919, 1 January: the Byelorussian Soviet republic is proclaimed in Smolensk ("The next day" after the conference of 30-31 December 1918); the seat moves to Minsk on 7 January 1919.
1919, 7 January: the seat moves from Smolensk to Minsk.
1919, 30 January: renamed the Soviet Socialist Republic of Byelorussia (SSRB) after separation from the Russian SFSR.

1919, 28 February: the Bolsheviks decide to merge the Lithuanian and Byelorussian republics into the Lithuanian-Belorussian SSR (Litbel); the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates are transferred to the RSFSR and the Gomel Governorate is created on 26 April.
1919, February-April: the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates pass to the RSFSR (the page ties the transfer to the Litbel decision of 28 February; no day).
1919, 8 August: Polish forces capture Minsk and the capital is evacuated to Smolensk the same day.
1919, 8 August: Minsk falls to Poland in the Polish-Soviet War.
1920, 31 July: the republic is re-established in Minsk (the page gives the date, not the military operation).

1921, 18 March: the Treaty of Riga ends the Polish-Soviet War; Poland recognises Soviet Belarus, withdraws from "areas further east, notably Minsk" and keeps western Belarus; the republic left is 52,400 km2 (the BSSR page dates the treaty February 1921).
1922, 30 December: the Byelorussian republic signs the Treaty on the Creation of the USSR with the Russian, Ukrainian and Transcaucasian republics and becomes a constituent republic of the Union.
1924, March: Russia returns most of the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates and parts of Smolensk to the republic, doubling it to 110,600 km2.
1926, 6 December: parts of the RSFSR's Gomel Governorate, including Gomel and Rechytsa, are added; the area rises to 126,300 km2.
1939, 17 September: the Soviet Union invades Poland from the east.
1939, 28 September: the German-Soviet demarcation treaty gives the Soviet Union "almost all Polish territory east of the line of the rivers Pisa, Narew, Western Bug and San".

1939, 15 November (infobox; the Soviet occupation began in September): the former Polish territories are "incorporated into the Belarusian SSR", except Vilnius and its surroundings, which go to Lithuania.
1941, summer: "Belarus was occupied by Nazi Germany"; much of the territory becomes the General District Belarus within Reichskommissariat Ostland.
1991, 25 August: Belarus declares independence (the republic is renamed the Republic of Belarus on 19 September 1991; sovereignty had been declared on 27 July 1990).

wars.name: Polish-Soviet War
wars.outcome: Poland takes Minsk on 8 August 1919; the Red Army re-establishes the republic in Minsk on 31 July 1920; Treaty of Riga (18 March 1921) leaves western Belarus with Poland.

certainty.note: Civil and Polish-Soviet war front; the republic held cities.
The Riga line (1921), the 1924 and 1926 transfers, and the 1939 demarcation are dated lines.
